For a sequential transducer $S$ with start state $s$, initial output $\iota$ and final output map $\phi$, and a word $x$, let $\delta_S(s, x)$ be the state $S$ reaches by reading $x$ from $s$ and $\lambda_S(s, x)$ the concatenation of the words it emits along the way, and call the concatenation…

nodes.summary: Let $S_1$ be a sequential transducer from $I$ to $M$ and $S_2$ one from $M$ to $O$, with start states $s_1$ and $s_2$. For a transducer $S$, a state $q$ and a word $w$, write $\delta_S(q, w)$ for the state $S$ reaches by reading $w$ from $q$ and $\lambda_S(q, w)$ for the concatenation of the words it emits along the way (without initial or final output); juxtaposition of words is concatenation. For a word $x$ over…

For a transducer $S$, a state $q$ and a word $w$, write $\lambda_S(q, w)$ for the concatenation of the words $S$ emits while reading $w$ from $q$ (without initial or final output). Then for all states $q_1$ of $S_1$ and $q_2$ of $S_2$ and every word $x$ over $I$,…

For a transducer $S$, a state $q$ and a word $w$, write $\delta_S(q, w)$ for the state $S$ reaches by reading $w$ from $q$ and $\lambda_S(q, w)$ for the concatenation of the words it emits along the way (without initial or final output); juxtaposition of words is concatenation. For a word $x$ over…

For a transducer $S$, a state $q$ and a word $w$, write $\delta_S(q, w)$ for the state $S$ reaches by reading $w$ from $q$ and $\lambda_S(q, w)$ for the concatenation of the words it emits along the way (without initial or final output). Then for all states $q_1$ of $S_1$ and $q_2$ of $S_2$ and every word $x$…
nodes.title: States reached by a composite sequential transducer

nodes.summary: Let $S_1$ be a sequential transducer from $I$ to $M$, $S_2$ one from $M$ to $O$, and $C$ their composition. Let $q_1$ be a state of $S_1$, $q_2$ a state of $S_2$ and $a \in I$ a letter, and suppose that $S_1$, reading $a$ in state $q_1$, moves to $q_1'$ and emits the word $w$. Then $C$, reading $a$ in state $(q_1, q_2)$, moves to $(q_1', q_2')$, where $q_2'$ is the state $S_2$ reaches by reading $w$ from $q_2$.
nodes.title: One step of a composite transducer: the successor state

nodes.summary: Let $S_1$ be a sequential transducer from $I$ to $M$, $S_2$ one from $M$ to $O$, and $C$ their composition. Let $q_1$ be a state of $S_1$, $q_2$ a state of $S_2$ and $a \in I$ a letter, and let $w$ be the word $S_1$ emits when it reads $a$ in state $q_1$. Then the word $C$ emits when it reads $a$ in state $(q_1, q_2)$ is the concatenation of the words $S_2$ emits while reading $w$ from $q_2$.
nodes.title: One step of a composite transducer: the output

nodes.summary: Let $S_1$ be a sequential transducer from $I$ to $M$ with start state $s_1$, initial output $\iota_1$ and final output map $\phi_1$, and let $S_2$ be one from $M$ to $O$ with start state $s_2$, initial output $\iota_2$ and final output map $\phi_2$. For a transducer $S$, a state $q$ and a word $w$, write $\delta_S(q, w)$ for the state $S$ reaches by reading $w$ from $q$ and $\lambda_S(q, w)$ for the concatenation…
nodes.title: Composition of sequential transducers

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a sequential transducer with finitely many states, input alphabet $I$ and output alphabet $O$, and let $L$ be a regular language over $O$. Then the preimage of $L$ under $S$, the set of words over $I$ that $S$ translates to some word of $L$, is regular.
nodes.title: Inverse sequential transduction preserves regular languages

nodes.summary: A Mealy machine with state set $Q$, input alphabet $I$ and output alphabet $O$ consists of a start state in $Q$ and a transition function that, given a state $q \in Q$ and an input letter $a \in I$, returns a successor state in $Q$ and a single output letter in $O$; thus the output of a transition depends on the state and the input letter.
nodes.title: Mealy machine

nodes.summary: A Moore machine with state type $Q$, input alphabet $\Sigma$ and output alphabet $\Gamma$ consists of a transition function, assigning to each state $q$ and input letter $a$ a successor state $\delta(q, a) \in Q$, an output function $\lambda : Q \to \Gamma$, and a start state $q_0 \in Q$. The output depends only on the state.
nodes.title: Moore machine

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a sequential transducer with output alphabet $\Gamma$ and let $M$ be a DFA over $\Gamma$. The language accepted by the product DFA of $S$ and $M$ equals the preimage under $S$ of the language accepted by $M$, that is, the set of input words that $S$ translates to some word accepted by $M$.
nodes.title: The product DFA recognizes the preimage

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a sequential transducer and $M$ a DFA over the output alphabet of $S$. For every input word $x$, state $q$ of $S$ and state $r$ of $M$, the product DFA of $S$ and $M$, started in $(q, r)$ and run on $x$, ends in the state $(q', r')$, where $q'$ is the final state of the run of $S$ from $q$ on $x$ and $r'$ is the state that $M$ reaches from $r$ on the output word of that run.
nodes.title: Runs of the product DFA

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a sequential transducer with state type $Q$, input alphabet $\Sigma$ and output alphabet $\Gamma$, and let $M$ be a DFA over $\Gamma$ with state type $P$. The product DFA of $S$ and $M$ is the DFA over $\Sigma$ with state type $Q \times P$ defined as follows. In state $(q, r)$ on a letter $a$, if $S$ moves from $q$ to $q'$ emitting the word $w$, it moves to $(q', r')$, where $r'$ is the state $M$ reaches…
nodes.title: Product DFA of a sequential transducer and a DFA

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a sequential transducer with input alphabet $\Sigma$ and output alphabet $\Gamma$, and let $L$ be a language over $\Gamma$. The preimage of $L$ under $S$ is the language over $\Sigma$ consisting of the words $x$ for which there is a word $y \in L$ such that $S$ translates $x$ to $y$.
nodes.title: Preimage of a language under a sequential transducer

nodes.summary: The run of a Mealy machine $M$ from a state $q$ on an input word $a_1 \cdots a_n$ is the pair $(q_n, o_1 \cdots o_n)$, where $q_0 = q$ and, for each $1 \le i \le n$, $M$ moves from $q_{i-1}$ on $a_i$ to $q_i$ emitting the output letter $o_i$.
nodes.title: Run of a Mealy machine

nodes.summary: The run of a Moore machine $M$ with output function $\lambda$ from a state $q$ on an input word $a_1 \cdots a_n$ is the pair $(q_n, \lambda(q_0) \lambda(q_1) \cdots \lambda(q_n))$, where $q_0 = q$ and, for each $1 \le i \le n$, $q_i$ is the successor of $q_{i-1}$ on $a_i$. The output word has $n + 1$ letters and begins with the output of the starting state.
nodes.title: Run of a Moore machine

nodes.summary: The run of a sequential transducer $S$ from a state $q$ on an input word $a_1 \cdots a_n$ is the pair $(q_n, w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n)$, where $q_0 = q$ and, for each $1 \le i \le n$, $S$ moves from $q_{i-1}$ on $a_i$ to $q_i$ emitting the word $w_i$. The initial output and the final outputs of $S$ are not included.
nodes.title: Run of a sequential transducer

nodes.summary: For a Mealy machine $M$, a state $q$ and an input word $x$, the output word of $M$ from $q$ on $x$ is the second component of the run of $M$ from $q$ on $x$: the word of output letters emitted along that run, one per input letter.
nodes.title: Output word of a Mealy machine run

nodes.summary: For a Moore machine $M$, a state $q$ and an input word $x$, the output word of $M$ from $q$ on $x$ is the second component of the run of $M$ from $q$ on $x$: the outputs of the states visited along that run, starting with the output of $q$; it has one more letter than $x$.
nodes.title: Output word of a Moore machine run

nodes.summary: For a sequential transducer $S$, a state $q$ and input words $x$ and $y$, the output word of the run of $S$ from $q$ on $xy$ is the output word of the run from $q$ on $x$ followed by the output word of the run on $y$ from the final state of the run from $q$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Output of a sequential transducer on a concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Mealy machine, $q$ a state, $a$ an input letter and $x$ an input word, and let $q'$ and $o$ be the successor state and the output letter of $M$ in state $q$ on letter $a$. The output word of the run of $M$ from $q$ on $ax$ is $o$ followed by the output word of the run from $q'$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Output of a Mealy machine on a nonempty word

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Moore machine, $q$ a state, $a$ an input letter and $x$ an input word, and let $q'$ be the successor state of $M$ in state $q$ on letter $a$. The output word of the run of $M$ from $q$ on $ax$ is the output of $q$ followed by the output word of the run from $q'$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Output of a Moore machine on a nonempty word

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a sequential transducer, $q$ a state, $a$ an input letter and $x$ an input word, and let $q'$ and $w$ be the successor state and the output word of $S$ in state $q$ on letter $a$. The output word of the run of $S$ from $q$ on $ax$ is $w$ followed by the output word of the run from $q'$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Output of a sequential transducer on a nonempty word

nodes.summary: For a Moore machine $M$, a state $q$ and an input word $x$, the output word of the run of $M$ from $q$ on $x$ is the output of $q$ followed by the output word of the run of the sequential rendering of $M$ from $q$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Moore machine output via its sequential rendering

nodes.summary: For a sequential transducer $S$, a state $q$ and an input word $x$, the output word of the run from $q$ on $x$ is the concatenation of the output words that $S$ emits on the successive letters of $x$, starting in $q$ and moving to the successor state after each letter; the initial and final outputs are not included.
nodes.title: Output word of a sequential transducer run

nodes.summary: For a Mealy machine $M$, a state $q$ and an input word $x$, the final state of the run from $q$ on $x$ is the state reached by starting in $q$ and moving, on each successive letter of $x$, to the successor state given by the transition function of $M$; on the empty word it is $q$.
nodes.title: Final state of a Mealy machine run

nodes.summary: For a Moore machine $M$, a state $q$ and an input word $x$, the final state of the run from $q$ on $x$ is the state reached by starting in $q$ and moving, on each successive letter of $x$, to the successor state given by the transition function of $M$; on the empty word it is $q$.
nodes.title: Final state of a Moore machine run

nodes.summary: For a sequential transducer $S$, a state $q$ and input words $x$ and $y$, the final state of the run of $S$ from $q$ on $xy$ is the final state of the run on $y$ from the final state of the run from $q$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Final state of a sequential transducer on a concatenation

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Mealy machine, $q$ a state, $a$ an input letter and $x$ an input word, and let $q'$ be the successor state of $M$ in state $q$ on letter $a$. The final state of the run of $M$ from $q$ on $ax$ is the final state of the run from $q'$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Final state of a Mealy machine on a nonempty word

nodes.summary: For a Moore machine $M$ with transition function $\delta$, a state $q$, an input letter $a$ and an input word $w$, the final state of the run of $M$ from $q$ on the word $aw$ equals the final state of the run of $M$ from $\delta(q, a)$ on $w$.
nodes.title: Final state of a Moore machine run on a nonempty word

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a sequential transducer, $q$ a state, $a$ an input letter and $w$ an input word, and let $q'$ be the successor state of $q$ on $a$ under the transition function of $S$. Then the final state of the run of $S$ from $q$ on the word $aw$ equals the final state of the run of $S$ from $q'$ on $w$.
nodes.title: Final state of a sequential transducer run on a nonempty word

nodes.summary: For a sequential transducer $S$, a state $q$ and an input word $w$, the final state of the run of $S$ from $q$ on $w$ is obtained by starting in $q$, reading the letters of $w$ in order, moving at each letter to the successor state given by the transition function of $S$, and taking the state reached at the end.
nodes.title: Final state of a sequential transducer run

nodes.summary: For a Mealy machine $M$, a state $q$ and an input word $w$, the output word of the run from $q$ on $w$ of the sequential transducer associated with $M$ (excluding its initial and final outputs) equals the output word of the run of $M$ from $q$ on $w$.
nodes.title: The sequential transducer of a Mealy machine has the same run outputs

nodes.summary: For a Mealy machine $M$, a state $q$ and an input word $w$, the final state of the run from $q$ on $w$ of the sequential transducer associated with $M$ equals the final state of the run of $M$ from $q$ on $w$.
nodes.title: The sequential transducer of a Mealy machine has the same final states

nodes.summary: A sequential transducer with states in a type $Q$, input letters in a type $\Sigma$ and output letters in a type $\Gamma$ consists of a transition function assigning to each state $q \in Q$ and input letter $a \in \Sigma$ a successor state in $Q$ and an output word over $\Gamma$, a start state in $Q$, a set of accepting states $F \subseteq Q$, an initial output word over $\Gamma$, and, for each state in $Q$, a…
nodes.title: Sequential transducer

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Moore machine with transition function $\delta$, output function $\lambda$ and start state $q_0$. Its sequential transducer has the same states and the start state $q_0$; reading a letter $a$ in state $q$ it moves to $\delta(q, a)$ and emits the one-letter word $\lambda(\delta(q, a))$; every state is accepting; the initial output is the one-letter word $\lambda(q_0)$; and every final output is empty.
nodes.title: The sequential transducer of a Moore machine

nodes.summary: For a Moore machine $M$, the set of accepting states of the sequential transducer associated with $M$ is the set of all states.
nodes.title: Every state of the sequential transducer of a Moore machine is accepting

nodes.summary: For a Mealy machine $M$, the set of accepting states of the sequential transducer associated with $M$ is the set of all states.
nodes.title: Every state of the sequential transducer of a Mealy machine is accepting

nodes.summary: For a Moore machine $M$ and every state $q$, the final output word at $q$ of the sequential transducer associated with $M$ is empty.
nodes.title: Final outputs of the sequential transducer of a Moore machine

nodes.summary: For every Mealy machine $M$ and every state $q$, the final output of the sequential transducer of $M$ at $q$ is the empty word.
nodes.title: Final outputs of the sequential transducer of a Mealy machine

nodes.summary: For every Moore machine $M$, the initial output of the sequential transducer of $M$ is the one-letter word consisting of the output of the start state of $M$.
nodes.title: Initial output of the sequential transducer of a Moore machine

nodes.summary: For every Mealy machine $M$, the initial output of the sequential transducer of $M$ is the empty word.
nodes.title: Initial output of the sequential transducer of a Mealy machine

nodes.summary: The sequential transducer of a Mealy machine $M$ has the states and the start state of $M$; on an input letter $a$ in a state $q$ it moves to the state that $M$ moves to and emits the one-letter word consisting of the letter that $M$ outputs on this transition. Every state accepts, and the initial and final outputs are empty.
nodes.title: Mealy machine as a sequential transducer

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Moore machine with start state $q_0$, and write $o(q)$ for the output of a state $q$. On an input word $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$, let $q_i$ be the state that $M$ moves to from $q_{i-1}$ on $a_i$. The transduction of $M$ on this word is the output word $o(q_0)\, o(q_1) \cdots o(q_n)$, of length $n + 1$.
nodes.title: Transduction of a Moore machine

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Mealy machine with start state $q_0$. On an input word $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$, for each $i$ let $q_i$ and $b_i$ be the state that $M$ moves to and the letter that it outputs when it reads $a_i$ in state $q_{i-1}$. The transduction of $M$ on this word is the output word $b_1 b_2 \cdots b_n$.
nodes.title: Transduction of a Mealy machine

nodes.summary: Let $S_1$ be a sequential transducer from an alphabet $A$ to an alphabet $B$, and $S_2$ one from $B$ to an alphabet $C$. For every word $x$ over $A$ and every word $y$ over $C$, the composition of $S_1$ and $S_2$ translates $x$ to $y$ if and only if there is a word $z$ over $B$ such that $S_1$ translates $x$ to $z$ and $S_2$ translates $z$ to $y$.
nodes.title: Translations of a composite sequential transducer

nodes.summary: For every Moore machine $M$, input word $x$ and output word $y$, the sequential transducer of $M$ translates $x$ to $y$ if and only if the transduction of $M$ on $x$ is $y$.
nodes.title: The sequential transducer of a Moore machine computes its transduction

nodes.summary: For every Mealy machine $M$, input word $x$ and output word $y$, the sequential transducer of $M$ translates $x$ to $y$ if and only if the transduction of $M$ on $x$ is $y$.
nodes.title: The sequential transducer of a Mealy machine computes its transduction

nodes.summary: A sequential transducer $S$ translates an input word $x$ to an output word $y$ when the run of $S$ on $x$ from its start state ends in an accepting state $q$ and $y$ is the concatenation of the initial output of $S$, the output words emitted by the transitions along the run, and the final output of $S$ at $q$.
nodes.title: Translation by a sequential transducer

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
